Help-center excerpts:

[support-complaints] Making a complaint (effective 2025-01-01)
If you're unhappy with something we've done, tell us. You can make a formal complaint at any time.

## How to complain

Message support in the app and say you'd like to make a formal complaint. Tell us what happened and what you'd like us to do. Support will pass it to our Complaints team.

## What happens next

- We acknowledge your complaint within 2 business days.
- We send a final response within 15 business days.

If we need more time, for example because we're waiting on another bank, we'll tell you why and when to expect an

[disputes-unauthorized] Disputing a transaction you didn't make (effective 2026-01-15)
of each month. For example, a transaction that posted in March appears on the March statement, so the window runs from the end of March.

## What happens next

- If your dispute passes an initial review, you get a provisional credit within 10 business days.
- Most investigations finish within 45 days. Foreign transactions, and accounts open less than 30 days, can take up to 90 days.

## Your liability

You aren't responsible for unauthorized card transactions reported within the window.

## Not sure it's unauthorized?

Unfamiliar names are often a

[disputes-provisional-credit] Provisional credit during a dispute (effective 2025-01-01)
it can take up to 90 days.

## If the dispute goes your way

The provisional credit becomes permanent. You don't need to do anything.

## If it doesn't

We send you a written explanation and take the provisional credit back 5 business days after that notice. If that makes your balance negative, you'll need to add money.

Not every dispute gets a provisional credit. For example, we may wait for the merchant's response if you already received a refund for part of the purchase.

Still stuck? Chat with us in the app. Someone is there around the

[support-complaints] Making a complaint (effective 2025-01-01)
waiting on another bank, we'll tell you why and when to expect an answer.

## Our response

The final response explains what we found, what we'll do, and your options if you're still unhappy, including where you can take your complaint outside Tallowbrook.

## Legal matters

If your message involves legal action or a regulator, support passes it straight to the Complaints team.

Making a complaint never affects how we treat your account.

Still stuck? Chat with us in the app. Someone is there around the clock.

[disputes-status] Checking the status of a dispute (effective 2025-01-01)
**Resolved in your favor:** the credit is permanent.
- **Denied:** we've sent an explanation, and any provisional credit will be taken back.

## How long it takes

Most disputes finish within 45 days, and some take up to 90 days. We'll message you whenever the status changes.

## Adding information

You can upload documents or add notes to an open dispute from the case page at any time.

## Cancelling a dispute

If the merchant refunds you directly, withdraw the dispute from the case page so you aren't credited twice. If you were credited twice,

[disputes-provisional-credit] Provisional credit during a dispute (effective 2025-01-01)
A provisional credit is money we put back in your account while we investigate a dispute. It lets you use the money without waiting for the final outcome.

## When you get it

If your dispute passes an initial review, the provisional credit arrives within 10 business days of filing. It shows in your activity as "Provisional credit" with the merchant name.

How long you have

File a merchant dispute within 90 days of the transaction date. After that, we can't open a dispute for you.

## How to file

Tap the transaction, then Get help, then Problem with a purchase. Tell us what happened and upload your records.

## What happens next

If the dispute passes an initial review, you get a provisional credit within 10 business days. We then contact the merchant through the card network. Most cases finish within 45 days.

Customer question:
How long does it take to get a response to a formal complaint?

request.instructions:
You are the help-center assistant for Tallowbrook, a US neobank. Answer the customer's question using only the help-center excerpts you are given.

Rules:
- Use only facts stated in the excerpts. Do not add fees, limits, dates, steps or products they do not mention.
- Some excerpts are older versions of a policy. When two excerpts disagree, follow the one with the later effective date.
- If the question depends on the customer's plan (Basic, Plus or Premium), use that plan's numbers.
- If the question rests on something false (for example a fee that does not exist), say so and give the correct facts. That is an answer, not an abstention.
- Abstain when the excerpts do not contain the answer, when the question is not about Tallowbrook, or when it asks for investment, tax or legal advice. Set "abstain" to true and say briefly that the help center does not cover it.
- Cite the article IDs (the text in square brackets) of every excerpt you used. Cite nothing when you abstain.
- Keep the answer short: two to four sentences, plain language.
